tools.name: gate_openshell_setup
tools.description: Read-only local setup plan for native OpenShell + Gate: one command, exact installer hash, recipe schema, prerequisites, authority boundaries and cleanup. Default creates an isolated Free read-only demo with no model or payment. A trusted local controller may configure an owner-authorized API with e

tools.name: gate_create_project
tools.description: Put Odile Gate in front of an existing HTTPS API. Returns project_id, admin_key (shown once) and the gateway base URL apps call instead of the API.

tools.name: gate_add_app
tools.description: Give one app its own key and the calls it may make. Routes are rules like "GET /orders/:id", "POST /orders", "GET /users/{user}/orders" (per-user), or example calls like "GET /orders/42", which become rules. Returns the app key (shown once).

tools.name: gate_list_apps
tools.description: The project's apps with their allowed calls, limits, state and anomaly-guard settings.

tools.name: gate_check_setup
tools.description: Read actual Gate protection settings before giving an integration production access. Reports observe-only mode, writes without mandatory runs, missing user-token configuration, wildcard grants and approval separation, with evidence, exact remedies and explicit limits. Sends no upstream requests, cha

tools.name: gate_metrics
tools.description: Read last-24-hour stored call counts by HTTP status and reason, measured duration through response headers (including upstream wait), per-app anomaly scores and 24-hour anomaly counts, and separate current-month gateway usage. Project admin only. Audit may be partial: invalid-key sampling and audit-

tools.name: gate_audit
tools.description: The most recent calls through the gateway (time, app, matched route, status, reason, duration), newest first, with totals by status and refusal reason. Gate never stores bodies, query values or headers.

tools.name: gate_create_run
tools.description: Gate Actions: give one agent session narrow, expiring permission. Actions are rules with {placeholders} bound by scope (e.g. "PATCH /customers/{customer}/tickets/:id" with scope {"customer":"A"}), each with an optional max and approval. Returns a run token (shown once) the agent sends as x-odile-run

tools.name: gate_set_app_runs
tools.description: Make an app need a run: "writes" (every write needs x-odile-run), "all" (every call), or "off".

tools.name: gate_set_response
tools.description: Opt-in JSON response redaction: return only explicit JSON Pointer paths, e.g. /id and /items/*/name. * matches one segment; selecting a container allows its whole subtree. Applies to every upstream response for this app, including errors. Maximum 1 MiB and 5 seconds to read; invalid/non-JSON respons

tools.name: gate_add_approver
tools.description: Create an approver key for the person who approves held actions (shown once). Give it to that person, never to an agent: once a project has an approver, the admin key can no longer approve.

tools.name: gate_list_actions
tools.description: Actions waiting for approval (or in another state), with the exact call. With an installed approval-risk model, pending actions sort by risk descending and include risk (0–1) and risk_features (top two advisory signals). No model means no score and newest first. Only a person decides in the dashboar

tools.name: gate_explain_refusal
tools.description: What a Gate refusal means and how to fix it, from the x-gate-refused header value (e.g. route_not_allowed).

tools.name: gate_delegate_run
tools.description: Hand a narrower run to another active app in the same project. Uses the parent app key and run token, never the admin key. Scope, expiry, approvals and ancestor budgets stay enforced; maximum depth five.

tools.name: gate_learn_suggestions
tools.description: Read normalized routes and a suggested per-minute limit from an admin-enabled, time-boxed learning session. Records only method, normalized path templates and counts per minute; no query values, raw ids, headers or bodies. Never enables learning or applies rules.

tools.name: gate_audit_proof
tools.description: Read chained audit rows, decided-action feature snapshots and anchors with an HMAC-SHA256 signature. No sealed paths/bodies, notes, keys or IPs in the action labels. Legacy actions lack snapshots and are excluded. store_audit=false has no chain. Follow next_from for audit rows and next_actions_after

tools.name: gate_audit_verify
tools.description: Recompute a pasted export chain and project signature; returns intact or broken_at (one-based row position). Does not approve actions or change permissions.

tools.name: gate_run_tree
tools.description: Read a run and its delegated descendants without tokens.

tools.name: gate_run_timeline
tools.description: Read call metadata, approvals and approver names, recovery outcomes and delegated children; no bodies or query values.

tools.name: gate_validate_config
tools.description: Parse and check a declarative Gate config (apps, routes, rate limits, run mode, plugins including anomaly-guard, alerts, approvers) without changing anything. anomaly-guard settings: mode off|alert|strict, z_threshold 2–10, min_minutes 1–30, half_life 5–1440. Returns errors with their path, warnings

tools.name: gate_sync_declarative
tools.description: Make a Gate project match an odile.yaml: creates the project (if no project_id) and missing apps and approvers, applies run mode, loop, learning and anomaly-guard settings and alerts. Example plugin: {name: anomaly-guard, settings: {mode: alert, z_threshold: 4, min_minutes: 3, half_life: 60}}. Never

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: gate_add_app, gate_create_run · Private data: gate_openshell_setup, gate_check_setup, gate_create_run, gate_delegate_run, gate_learn_suggestions, gate_run_tree · Public sink: gate_add_app, gate_create_run · Destructive: gate_openshell_setup, gate_create_run, gate_set_app_runs, gate_delegate_run, gate_run_tree, gate_run_timeline, gate_validate_config, gate_sync_declarative.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: gate_add_app, gate_create_run · Private data: gate_openshell_setup, gate_check_setup, gate_create_run, gate_delegate_run, gate_learn_suggestions, gate_run_tree · Public sink: gate_add_app, gate_create_run · Destructive: gate_openshell_setup, gate_create_run, gate_set_app_runs, gate_delegate_run, gate_run_tree, gate_run_timeline, gate_validate_config, gate_sync_declarative

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
